title: Tested SST step corrections reduce the AMIP radiation-trend gap but increase its feedback gap in 2001-2022
abstract: We compared PCMDI-AMIP 1.1.9 and the CMIP7Plus OI2p1 1.0 prototype on 29,162 fixed ice-free ocean cells. We applied published SST step maps and five model Green functions. For 2001-2022 the raw five-model mean new-minus-old radiation trend is -0.1562 W m-2 per decade. Across 40 tested correction pairs, its size falls by 7-39%. But the feedback gap, defined as the difference of radiation-trend to SST-trend ratios, grows by a factor of 1.45-2.17. The old-file correction changes its SST trend much more than its mean radiation trend. Over 1982-2022 both gap sizes fall. Thus the response depends on the measure and time interval. Twelve source checks give masked mean prototype-minus-OISST differences below 0.0024 K, but spatial errors are larger. Correction maps, half-size tests and conditional block intervals do not cover all source uncertainty. This is a linear sensitivity test, not a new atmosphere simulation or proof of true corrected SST. Code, aggregate evidence and exact retrieval records are included.
